chapter: San Francisco, the So Different Orchestra and Johnny
title: Slocum Mitchell's clarinet style and its influence
summary: Slocum Mitchell from Martinique made wailing sounds on clarinet that Spikes says Armstrong and King Oliver later picked up; he never recorded.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: that, you know, slurring and things on their trumpets and things from him.

No, no, none of us recorded in those days, you know. So, and, uh...he was doing all that stuff... A lot of people nearly trip over when they pass the bandstand sometime, and he'd be playing [vocally imitates Slocum's instrumental style]-- you know, making all that jazz stuff and everything, and it'd frighten them and they'd tickled and turn around and look at it and see what was going on, and they nearly run over something. And when he's playing the blues, oh, it was a sensation, you know. The blues was very popular in those days.
